# AI & Machine Learning / Classical Machine Learning

Frame ML problems, engineer and select features, train and tune scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost models, cluster and reduce dimensions, validate without leakage, explain models with SHAP, PDP, LIME and counterfactuals, and build forecasting, survival, recommendation, ranking, fraud and uplift models.

## Problem framing

| Skill | What it does | Scripts |
|-------|--------------|---------|
| [ml-problem-framing-advisor](ml-problem-framing-advisor/SKILL.md) | Turn a vague business ask ("use AI to reduce churn", "predict demand", "find fraud") into a precise, buildable ML problem: the decision and action the prediction drives, who acts and with what capacity, the unit and moment of prediction, the label with its observation and outcome windows, label delay, features available at prediction time, task type (binary, multiclass, ordinal, regression, count, forecasting, ranking, anomaly, clustering, uplift), the baseline to beat and the metric at the operating point. Flags leakage-by-framing, proxy labels, feedback loops, selection bias and unactionable predictions. | `frame_check.py`, `target_profile.py` |
| [ml-feasibility-assessor](ml-feasibility-assessor/SKILL.md) | Decide GO, GO WITH RISKS or NO-GO for an ML project before building it: enough labelled rows and minority examples, events per feature, label quality and coverage, history length and drift, single-feature signal (out-of-fold AUC / Spearman) and suspicious near-perfect predictors, data availability at prediction time, latency and serving constraints, the value ceiling given action capacity, and the cost of being wrong. Includes sample-size arithmetic for metric confidence intervals, AUC standard errors (Hanley-McNeil), McNemar test sizes and data collection time. | `feasibility_scan.py`, `sample_size.py` |
| [ml-baseline-model-builder](ml-baseline-model-builder/SKILL.md) | Build the baselines every ML model must beat before anyone trusts it: dummy majority/prior/mean/median predictors, the current business rule, a one-feature model (OneR), seasonal-naive and last-value forecasts, popularity recommenders, and a first honest linear model and HistGradientBoosting inside a leak-free scikit-learn Pipeline with a time-ordered, grouped or stratified holdout. Reports ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, log loss, Brier, balanced accuracy, MAE, RMSE, R2 and WAPE side by side, and warns when a first baseline looks too good (leakage). | `baseline_scores.py`, `scaffold_baseline.py` |
| [ml-success-metric-selector](ml-success-metric-selector/SKILL.md) | Choose the metric that defines success for an ML model, and the guardrails around it, from the decision it serves: precision/recall@K for capacity-bound actions, expected cost at the cost-optimal threshold for asymmetric errors, PR-AUC vs ROC-AUC for rare events, log loss/Brier/ECE when probabilities are consumed, macro- vs weighted-F1 for multiclass, MAE vs RMSE vs WAPE vs MAPE vs Poisson deviance for regression, MASE/RMSSE and pinball loss for forecasts, NDCG/MRR/recall@k for ranking and recommendation, concordance for survival, Qini/AUUC for uplift. Computes the full metric panel from a predictions CSV (scikit-learn-identical numbers) and finds the cost-minimising threshold. | `metric_report.py`, `pick_metric.py` |

| [counterfactual-explanation-generator](counterfactual-explanation-generator/SKILL.md) | Generate counterfactual explanations and algorithmic recourse: the smallest realistic change to a row's features that changes the model's decision. Solves exact minimal-cost recourse for linear and logistic models (MAD-scaled L1 cost, immutable features, increase/decrease directions, bounds, integer and binary features, diverse alternatives, features every counterfactual must change, and a no-recourse finding when immutable features decide), generates DiCE counterfactuals for any scikit-learn model with constraints turned into permitted ranges and every result re-predicted, and validates counterfactuals from any method for constraint violations, implausible values, off-manifold rows, broken derived-feature relations and failure to flip the prediction. | `cf_validate.py`, `gen_dice_script.py`, `linear_counterfactual.py` |
